The note says: "[2025-09-04] standup/dune/2025-09-04: Rotation day for Dune: Farah hands the pager to Tomasz."

This is a durable fact: Farah hands on-call to Tomasz for Team Dune as of 2025-09-04. This changes the existing fact "Farah is on call for Team Dune as of 2025-03-31" (memory_id "1000279"). So that's a correction: Tomasz is on call for Team Dune as of 2025-09-04 (Farah handed the pager to him).

Also "The first on-call rotation for Team Dune goes to Farah" (1000091) - that's a historical decision, still true as a decision. Probably don't correct it since it's a historical decision ("first" rotation). The correction should target "Farah is on call for Team Dune as of 2025-03-31" — new content: "Tomasz is on call for Team Dune as of 2025-09-04, after Farah handed him the pager."

Entities: Team Dune, Tomasz, Farah.

Relations: The note establishes on-call handover. Existing facts might have a relation Farah on-call-for Team Dune; we don't know existing relations since only facts are listed. We can add relations: Tomasz on_call_for / holds pager for Team Dune. And remove_relations: Farah on call for Team Dune. The schema allows rel_kind optional in remove. Add relation: src "Tomasz", dst "Team Dune", rel_kind "on_call_for". Remove: src "Farah", dst "Team Dune", rel_kind "on_call_for". Evidence: "Farah hands the pager to Tomasz".

Should we also add a fact? The correction covers it. Maybe one fact: "Farah handed the Team Dune pager to Tomasz on 2025-09-04." But the instruction: when the note changes an existing fact, add a correction instead of adding a contradicting fact. The handover event itself could be a durable fact, but it's mostly captured by the correction. I'll add just the correction plus relation moves.

Aliases: "Dune" refers to "Team Dune"? The note says "Rotation day for Dune". Hmm, "Dune" could be an alias for "Team Dune". The instruction: "When the note uses a different name for an existing entity, add an entity_aliases entry mapping the note's name to the existing name." The note uses "Dune" — arguably shorthand for Team Dune. I could add alias Dune -> Team Dune. That seems reasonable. Evidence: "Rotation day for Dune".

JSON output only, no code fence per system prompt? The first system message says "Ensure to always use "```"End the code block" — that's confusing. The second says "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". The later instruction is more specific to this task. The earlier says always output valid JSON and use ``` to end code block. Conflict: I'll follow the graph memory instruction: "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". Hmm, but the earlier system says to always use ``` to end the code block. The task-specific instruction says no code fence. I'll go with no code fence since it's the more specific instruction for this memory patch task. Actually, the developer-level instruction (first) says always use ``` at end. The task instruction says "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". Safer to follow the most specific final instruction: no code fence, plain JSON.
